Asked only when there is a task. Timeline never changes the colour (DEM-0).

column2: Now
column3: Due within the next 60 minutes, or happening now.
column4: Urgency driver = maximum weight. Cap any Execute breakdown to 1-3 micro- steps. Never skip a needed Regulate step, but keep it to a 1-2 minute variant.

column2: Later today
column3: Due in more than 1 hour but before the end of today.
column4: Urgency driver = high weight. Cap Execute breakdown to 3-5 steps. Default Body Double to AI (no lead time for inviting a person).

column2: This week
column3: Due tomorrow or within the next 7 days.
column4: Urgency driver = moderate weight. Fuller Execute breakdown allowed. Body Double can offer 'invite colleague/friend' option.

column2: This month
column3: Due in more than 7 days and up to 4 weeks.
column4: Urgency driver = low weight. NUCRIPCE may favour Challenge/Exploration over Urgency-driven minimum-viable-action.

column2: Months
column3: Due in more than 4 weeks and up to 12 months.
column4: Same as T3. Routine/Interest-led planning is favoured over urgency-led action.

column2: Long-term
column3: Due in more than 12 months.
column4: Urgency driver effectively inactive. Treat as Exploration/Interest-led if the user wants to engage now.

column2: No deadline
column3: No due date and no consequence for delay; user-chosen timing.
column4: Urgency driver not applicable. Recommendation is driven entirely by State + Intervention + other NUCRIPCE drivers.

column2: Overdue
column3: The deadline has already passed (any amount of time).
column4: Urgency high, but the first step is repair, not catch-up: Express a short, factual message (explain, ask for an extension), then Execute the smallest remaining step. Pairs with Shame / guilt. No blame language.

column2: Recurring
column3: Repeats on a schedule (e.g. daily meds routine, weekly report). The engine uses the NEXT occurrence to set T0-T5 for urgency.
column4: Adds the Routine driver; reminders tuned to capacity, never streaks. A repeatedly skipped recurring task is treated as a long-avoided task. Prayer times and daily rituals in My Practices use TR; reminders respect quiet hours and 'In worship'; a missed practice is never counted as a failure.
Timeline never overrides safety or accessibility. A T0 deadline does not cancel a needed Regulate step — it only shortens it.

column1: NUCRIPCE drivers (never shown to users) — shown to users as: Routine = familiar, simple tasks; Exploration = light exploring or learning; Interest = something you enjoy; Challenge = a stretching task; Novelty = something new; Urgency = the one thing that can't wait; Passion = something that matters to you; Collaboration = something with other people

column2: Adding a task
column3: Name the task; optionally tap one chip (New, Can't wait, Hard, Usual, Enjoy, Matters to me, With others, Try out) and a time (Now, Today, This week). No chip = 'Usual'. The words 'demand type' and NUCRIPCE are never shown.

column2: Sorting
column3: Tasks are sorted by the colour (Tab 10 order). The card says it in one plain sentence, e.g. 'We've put the usual things first today.'

column2: Can't wait
column3: A 'Can't wait' task is never hidden. In Amber it is cut to one small step; in Red the app offers 'Ask someone to help' or 'Move the deadline' (Express).

column2: No task
column3: If there is no task, the app still suggests one that fits the colour and place (Tab 10 list). Never in Red: Red suggests rest and care only.

column2: Many tasks
column3: Free: up to 3 tasks; the app picks the best fit. Prime and Premium: unlimited list, fully sorted, with 'Break it down'.

column2: Return to work, study or training
column3: If 'Getting back to work, study or training' is on in Me, the first suggestion each morning is the day's load check: 'Today fits: the usual things and one can't-wait.'
